text:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a windowed handoff experiment to decouple prefill vs decode batching on the canary pool. seeing intermittent KV cache churn and a 95th latency blip around 120ms for tail requests. details + logs below

aj: can you paste the window settings and token budgets you used?

maria: sure. config for the run: prefill_window_ms=12, decode_window_ms=40, prefill_token_budget=48, decode_token_budget=128, min_prefill_batch_tokens=4. routed small prefix-only requests into prefills only.

srinivas: interesting — KV churn usually comes from tiny prefill batches that prime unique keys, evicting hot entries. what does the KV_EVICT metric look like?

maria: KV_EVICT spiked ~3x at 15:07 UTC when traffic hit a short burst. sample log snippet: ```[15:07:12] req=0x7f2a prefill_tokens=3 decode_tokens=0 kv_evict=12 kernel_switch=triton_q8 -> triton_q4```

leo: hmm. two quick ideas: 1) add a tiny hold window to aggregate micro-prefills (e.g., delay 6ms if prefill_tokens < 8). 2) bump min_prefill_batch_tokens to 8 and let decode_window be longer so decode can absorb leftovers.

aj: +1 to the hold window. also, can we try token-shaper: allocate token budget proportional to seq_len_histogram instead of fixed budgets? that might avoid kernel thrash from odd batch shapes.

maria: ran a trace E2E: prefill-only path went fast but created many unique KV keys due to per-caller prefixes; decode path hit a kernel that doesn't like tiny batch shapes and forced a fallback. combined effect = more GPU context switches + KV churn.

perf-bot: deploybot: ALERT — canary rollout paused: 5.2% p95 latency regression vs baseline over 10m window :warning:

srinivas: ok let's be conservative. plan: (A) enable 6ms micro-hold on prefills when prefill_tokens < 8, (B) set min_prefill_batch_tokens=8, (C) dynamic token rebalance: scale decode_budget down if prefill backlog > X in queue to prevent token starvation.

maria: implementing A+B now in canary (branch: perf/windowed-prefill). will also add a KV priming guard to avoid allocating new keys for very short-lived prefixes (opt-in flag).

aj: for measurement, capture: per-kernel invocations, kernel_fill_size histogram, kv_insert_rate, kv_evict_rate, and per-request kernel_fallback boolean. need those to prove hypothesis.

maria: yes — added those metrics to the bench dashboard and tagged runs: https://bench/redwood/canary/1769991234 (internal). starting 24h A/B. will post a short summary tomorrow. :thumbsup:

leo: if the 6ms hold hurts p50, we can try a jittered hold or use adaptive hold only when KV_EVICT trending up. avoids penalizing steady steady workloads.

maria: good call. will gate adaptive hold behind kv_evict_rate > 2x baseline. thanks all — will update with the first 1h signal.

aj: also add a trace for a few failing requests so we can repro kernel switch path locally. small dumps are super helpful.

maria: done, added 10 traces to the issue. linking in the bench run and the PR.

srinivas: nice. if this reduces kernel fallback + kv churn, we should see p95 down and lower GPU kernel switch counts.

maria: closing for now — live canary running. will follow up with concrete numbers.
